newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Arafat in Switzerland for World Economic Forum.
newsitem.headline: Arafat in Switzerland for World Economic Forum.

text.p: Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat joined the Israeli and Egyptian leaders in the Swiss resort of Davos on Saturday for a weekend of informal contacts on the Middle East and on the world economy.

Arafat is expected to meet Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu during the World Economic Forum at Davos for the first time since they reached agreement last month on the West Bank town of Hebron.

Arafat, Netanyahu and Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak will appear together on a panel at a meeting of the forum on Sunday but a three-way summit has not been arranged, Egyptian and Israeli officials said.
A Palestinian minister said on Saturday that Arafat was taking complaints that Israel was not keeping up its side of peace deals with the PLO to the forum.

"We have of course written statements which the president will take with him to Davos...and we will submit it to the sponsors and of course to the international community," Education Minister Hanan Ashrawi told reporters in Gaza.

"We have taken a very clear decision that we will continue the renovation of homes and that Israel has no business preventing the renovation of homes in Hebron and we will continue all the plans in order to implement agreements."
Israel on January 17 handed 80 percent of the West Bank town of Hebron to Palestinian rule after months of acrimonious negotiations that strained Middle East peace efforts.
Palestinian lawmakers on Wednesday rejected an Israeli military order prohibiting Palestinians from renovating Arab buildings near Jewish enclaves. The enclaves are under Israeli control.
Arafat did not speak to reporters on arrival in Davos, where more than 1,000 business people, politicians and academics have gathered for the annual meeting.
Arafat's agenda also includes meetings with Swiss Foreign Minister Flavio Cotti on Saturday and U.N. Secretary General Kofi Annan on Sunday, the organisers said.
On Friday Palestinian negotiator Nabil Shaath said he did not think Arafat's talks with Netanyahu would tackle the substance of the next round of peace talks.
"It's only a half-hour meeting (between Arafat and Netanyahu), though it is the first since they signed the agreement. I hope it will open up new roads," he said.

"The main issues will be to speed up the peace process and to reduce the closure (of the Palestinian territories). We'd also like to see the eight negotiating committees resuming as quickly as possible," he added.
Shaath said the Palestinians had no objection to a three-way summit but both Netanyahu and Egyptian Foreign Minister Amr Moussa have said such a meeting is not planned.
